generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential 1..N per table, unique, never NULL; final PK set frozen before any child FK sampling.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Copy from the FINAL surviving parent PK set (after dedup, unique-drop, parent-without-child deletion, NULL application). Nullable FKs get NULL share from the compact DB (fallback ~0.1) and non-NULL rows; NULL FK values are exempt from parent-PK membership (SQL three-valued FK semantics).
generic_sampling_rules.integer_quantity: Uniform integer in [1, 20]; never 0 or negative.
generic_sampling_rules.decimal_amount: Uniform decimal in [0, 1000] rounded to 4 dp; non-negative.
generic_sampling_rules.decimal_rate: Uniform decimal in [0, 1] rounded to 4 dp.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_short_enum: Pick uniformly from the enum list in per_column_exceptions.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_name: Random first/last name from a small pool; near-duplicates allowed.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_like: Base literal plus near-variants (case change, one-char substitution, appended suffix); mix pool values with random strings so boundary literals appear in at least one row.
generic_sampling_rules.numeric_boundary: For each listed literal L, sample L-step, L, L+step with step 0.01 for decimals and 1 for integers.
generic_sampling_rules.distinct_duplicates: Allow 20-50% duplicate values on DISTINCT-targeted columns.
generic_sampling_rules.order_ties: Ensure at least two rows share the top rank value on ORDER/LIMIT-targeted columns.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: Per nullable column, compute the NULL share from the compact database's observed share for that column (fallback ~0.1); ensure at least one NULL row per nullable column; NOT NULL/PK columns never NULL; planted NULLs are never replaced to satisfy a rule; _ensure_null must be idempotent (count existing NULLs first, add only up to target share).
generic_sampling_rules.group_sizes: For a non-key column targeted with group_sizes, produce at least one group of size 1, one of size 2 and one of size >=3 on that column's values; verify post-condition by value counts; if table size < 6, still produce sizes 1 and 2 and report the achievable post-condition.
generic_sampling_rules.rows_with_different_values: For a column targeted with rows_with_different_values, group by the stated grouping key and ensure each group has >=2 rows with distinct values of the column; for FK columns choose alternate values from the parent PK set, never by arithmetic increment; verify post-condition and retry with a different delta on collision.
generic_sampling_rules.generation_order: Parents fully materialized (PK dedup, unique-drop, parent-without-child deletion, NULL application) before any child FK column is sampled; child FK values drawn only from the final surviving parent PK set; parent-without-child deletion selects an unreferenced parent row (never a referenced one); after the parent-without-child deletion block, re-run _final_pk_values and re-validate all children.
generic_sampling_rules.date_order_fixup: DATE_GE fix-up runs before NULL planting; NULL operands are exempt (three-valued logic); no row with both non-NULL operands violates the order.
generic_sampling_rules.fk_membership_assertion: Before writing, verify every non-NULL child FK value is in the final surviving parent PK set; on failure, resample the offending FK column from the current final_pk (or drop the row) and count it in rows_failed; never silently pass.

supporting_evidence.date_order: Customers rows 1-8 all have date_last_hire > date_became_customer; Bookings rows 1-8 all have booking_end_date > booking_start_date.
supporting_evidence.non_negative_amounts: All shown amount_payable, amount_of_discount, amount_outstanding, amount_of_refund, amount_due, amount_paid, booked_amount, daily_hire_cost, coupon_amount values are >= 0.
supporting_evidence.enums: Observed distinct values match the enum lists in per_column_exceptions.
supporting_evidence.group_sizes: Customers.first_name and Customers.date_last_hire are non-key columns where duplicate values are legal; Customers.customer_id is a PK and is excluded from group_sizes/duplicates.
supporting_evidence.comparison_boundary: Customers.coupon_id is a join predicate (column-vs-column), not a literal boundary; it is covered by the dependencies entry, not by per_column_exceptions.
supporting_evidence.fk_integrity: Review feedback: 105 FK violations traced to child FK sampling from mid-construction parent dict and PARENT_WITHOUT_CHILD deleting referenced parent row 0. Fixed by generation_order rule: parents finalized first, deletion selects unreferenced row only; plus fk_membership_assertion post-check.
supporting_evidence.null_share: Review feedback: observed NULL shares far above 0.1 (Products_for_Hire.product_name 14/24, Products_Booked.booked_count 18/89, Customers.last_name 15/53). Fixed by computing per-column NULL share from compact DB and making _ensure_null idempotent.
supporting_evidence.duplicate_share: Review feedback: spec.py over-applied DUPLICATE_SHARE to Customers.first_name, Customers.date_last_hire, Payments.booking_id; removed so spec.py mirrors per_column_exceptions (only Discount_Coupons.coupon_amount and Payments.payment_date).
supporting_evidence.group_sizes_min_size: Review feedback: _force_group_sizes required n>=6 and silently skipped smaller tables. Fixed by handling n in {3,4,5} and adding explicit post-generation assertion.
supporting_evidence.fk_different_values: Review feedback: _force_different_in_groups on Products_Booked.product_id used arithmetic increment, risking out-of-parent values. Fixed by choosing alternate values from parent PK set and adding FK-membership check.
supporting_evidence.cross_table_amounts: Review feedback: no cross-table amount formula verified; added explicit NOT REQUIRED entry to avoid over-constraining.

uncertainty: No formula linking Bookings amounts to Payments or Products_Booked was verified on all shown rows; only range/enum/order rules are stated. NULL shares are taken from the compact DB per column (fallback ~0.1). Generation order: Discount_Coupons, Products_for_Hire, Customers, Bookings, Payments, Products_Booked, View_Product_Availability; datetime floors for order rules are taken from already-built parent tables or samplers, never from a table dict mid-construction. Post-generation assertions required: FK membership (with resample/drop and rows_failed counting), group_sizes singleton/pair/triple (with achievable post-condition for n<6), rows_with_different_values >=2 distinct per group, boundary literals present, zero skipped rows. The exact cause of the 10 FK violations in chk_0007 must be reproduced and traced; the fk_membership_assertion rule is the safety net.
